# desktop

Linux/X11 desktop odds and ends: i3 theming, ibus input method, and the synchronised dark/light theme switcher.

---

## `desktop_find_windows`

Print the X window IDs whose class name matches a pattern.

**Usage**

```sh
desktop_find_windows <class-name>
```

**Examples**

```sh
desktop_find_windows Alacritty
```

**Requires** `xdotool`

**OS** Linux only &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/linux/desktop.sh:90`](../../modules/linux/desktop.sh#L90)

---

## `desktop_find_windows_by_title`

Print window IDs by matching the window *title* instead of its class. Slower, but it finds Electron apps that lie about their class.

**Usage**

```sh
desktop_find_windows_by_title <pattern>
```

**Examples**

```sh
desktop_find_windows_by_title Slack
```

**Requires** `wmctrl`

**OS** Linux only &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/linux/desktop.sh:101`](../../modules/linux/desktop.sh#L101)

## `desktop_i3_set_theme`

Apply an i3-style theme to ~/.i3/config and reload i3.

> **⚠ DANGER** — Rewrites your i3 config in place. Keep it in version control.

**Usage**

```sh
desktop_i3_set_theme [theme]
```

**Examples**

```sh
desktop_i3_set_theme archlinux
```

**Requires** `i3-style`

**OS** Linux only &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/linux/desktop.sh:61`](../../modules/linux/desktop.sh#L61)

**See also** `desktop_i3_list_themes`

## `desktop_probe_pointer`

Wait three seconds, then print where the mouse pointer is. Use it to re-measure the Slack coordinates below when they drift.

**Usage**

```sh
desktop_probe_pointer
```

**Examples**

```sh
desktop_probe_pointer
```

**Requires** `xdotool`

**OS** Linux only &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/linux/desktop.sh:113`](../../modules/linux/desktop.sh#L113)

## `desktop_theme_switch`

Switch every application to the named theme. Anything other than "light" or "bright" means dark.

**Usage**

```sh
desktop_theme_switch [dark|light]
```

**Examples**

```sh
desktop_theme_switch light
```

**Requires** `xdotool`, `wmctrl`

**OS** Linux only &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/linux/desktop.sh:209`](../../modules/linux/desktop.sh#L209)
